title: Ex 2.6 #3 · P ⇒ Q = (∼P) ∨ Q
prompt: Use a truth table to show that $P \Rightarrow Q$ and $(\sim P) \vee Q$ are logically equivalent: they have the same truth value in every row.
answer_format: No final answer box. Give the truth-table column of each statement as a column step (statement : T F T T, rows (P, Q) in the order TT, TF, FT, FF), or rewrite one statement into the other with expr steps, each equivalent to the one before.
hints: Make a helper column for ∼P, then or it with Q.
P ⇒ Q is false only when P is true and Q is false.
solution: $\sim P$ is F F T T, so $(\sim P) \vee Q$ is T F T T.
$P \Rightarrow Q$ is also T F T T.
The columns agree in every row, so the statements are logically equivalent.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses logical equivalence (Section 2.6).
